newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas ends firmer, but illiquidity aids gains.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas ends firmer, but illiquidity aids gains.

text.p: IPE natural gas futures ended firmer on Thursday, although the front month March slipped off highs towards the close.
March last traded at 12.1 pence a therm (p/th), up 0.165 p/th on the day, but off a session high of 12.3 p/th.
Total trading volumes reached 215 lots, up on Wednesday's 280, but lower than the record 465 lots that changed hands on Friday.

Apart from the front month, trade was concentrated in the summer. Deals were done in all months from June to October. All made gains, with June the star performer, climbing 0.5 p/th on the day to close at 11.850 p/th.
While IPE price gains mirrored climbs in the physical market, brokers said that a lack of liquidity also contributed.

"I think that a little of the activity in the mid-months was people taking positions who had maybe gone short earlier in the week and were forced to cover today. They might not have paid what they would have liked to," said one dealer.
But most agreed that prices had bottomed out after March dipped below 12 p/th on Wednesday.
"This afternoon has confirmed that we found some good support at the 12 level. I think we might start to climb a bit from here," said one broker.
